'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[2021 Kabul airport attack]]
***A [[suicide bombing|suicide bomber]] blows himself up at an entrance of the [[Hamid Karzai International Airport]] in [[Kabul]], killing at least 90 Afghan civilians and 13 [[United States Armed Forces|American servicemembers]]. More than 150 others are wounded. [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Khorasan Province|ISIL-KP]], who have threatened the airport in recent days, have claimed responsibility for the attack. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/afghanistan-kabul-airport-explosion-11629976397 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
**[[2021 evacuation from Afghanistan]]
***[[Operation Pitting]]
****[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|British Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] says that the [[United Kingdom]] will continue evacuations despite the [[terrorist]] attacks that occurred at [[Hamid Karzai International Airport]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/afghanistan-boris-johnson-says-uks-evacuation-operation-will-continue-despite-barbaric-kabul-attack-12391442 (Sky News)]
***[[Operation Allies Refuge]]
****[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]], in an [[Address to the Nation|address to the nation]], says that the evacuation of American citizens will continue despite the terrorist attacks. He also vows that the U.S. will avenge the deaths of the 13 [[United States Armed Forces|service members]] killed in the attacks by "hunting down" those responsible and "making them pay". [https://apnews.com/article/europe-evacuations-kabul-f9321f143fd8749c1cc8c460b647fdd5 (AP)]
****The United States says that it is taking steps to boost humanitarian aid into [[Afghanistan]] despite the Taliban being blacklisted by the treasury. The United States also says that it is working with local partners to facilitate humanitarian aid to reach the Afghan population. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us-taking-steps-allow-humanitarian-aid-afghanistan-continue-2021-08-26/ (Reuters)]
***[[Canada]], [[Belgium]], [[Denmark]], [[Russia]] and the [[Netherlands]] end their evacuation flights from [[Hamid Karzai International Airport]] ahead of a [[Taliban]] ultimatum to leave by August 31. Several shots are fired in the direction of an [[Italian Armed Forces|Italian]] [[military plane]] as it was departing the airport, although the airplane was not the intended target and no casualties or damage have been reported. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/world-58279900 (BBC News)]
*[[Oromo conflict]], [[Tigray War]], [[War crimes in the Tigray War]]
**The [[Ethiopian Human Rights Commission]] accuses the [[Oromo Liberation Army]] of killing 150 civilians during the past week. The group denies the report. The report says that gunmen targeted people of [[Amhara people|Amharan]] ethnicity. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ethiopia-rights-commission-says-150-killed-attack-oromiya-2021-08-26/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Political repression in the Soviet Union]]
**A [[mass grave]] containing between 5,000 and 8,000 skeletons is discovered in [[Odesa]], [[Ukraine]], during exploration works for a planned expansion of [[Odesa International Airport]]. The graves are believed to date back to the late 1930s during a major [[purge]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-58340805 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A three-story building [[structural integrity and failure|collapses]] in [[Peñíscola]], [[Valencian Community]], [[Spain]], killing two people and injuring another person. The reason for the collapse is currently unknown. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/08/26/two-people-killed-in-apartment-building-collapse-in-eastern-spain (Euronews)]
*At least 9 people are killed and more than 80 injured by an explosion at a [[Armed Forces of the Republic of Kazakhstan|military]] compound in southern [[Kazakhstan]]. The fire was caused by a fire at the ammunition depot. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/08/26/at-least-60-injured-in-explosion-at-ammunition-depot-in-kazakhstan (Euronews)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brunei]]
****[[Brunei]] reports its first cases of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant]], which was first detected in [[India]], in 20 samples of COVID-19 cases that were sent for [[genome sequencing]]. [https://thescoop.co/2021/08/26/brunei-reports-fourth-covid-19-death-in-three-days/ (The Scoop)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] suspends the usage of 1.63 million doses of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] due to concerns of [[contamination]] in some unused vials. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58338281 (BBC News)] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/japan-halts-some-moderna-vaccine-after-contamination-found/2021/08/26/5b906e1a-062e-11ec-b3c4-c462b1edcfc8_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 24,599 new cases and 393 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1.64 million and the nationwide death toll to 15,211. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/malaysia-record-covid-19-cases-deaths-aug-26-2137392 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia]]
****[[Mongolia]] surpasses 200,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://m.akipress.com/news:661863:Mongolia_confirmed_2,467_new_cases_of_coronavirus/ (AKI Press)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
****[[Sri Lanka]] reports a record 209 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 8,157. [https://economynext.com/record-209-covid-19-deaths-in-sri-lanka-taking-death-toll-to-8157-85488/ (EconomyNext)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 820 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 179,243. [https://www.barrons.com/amp/news/russia-reports-record-daily-virus-deaths-official-tally-01629968707 (''Barron's'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia]]
****The [[Slovenia]]n [[Government of Slovenia|government]] announces that university students and anyone under the age of 15 who is not vaccinated or who has not recovered from COVID-19 will have to be [[COVID-19 testing|tested]] once a week in order to enter a university or participate in indoor sports or recreational activities. [https://sloveniatimes.com/use-of-pct-rule-expanded-to-students-indoor-sports/ (''The Slovenia Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales]]
****[[New South Wales]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 1,029 cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the first time since the beginning of the [[pandemic]] that the state has reported more than 1,000 cases in a single day. [https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/world/2021/08/coronavirus-new-south-wales-records-more-than-1000-new-covid-19-cases.html (Newshub)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Honduras]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in Honduras]]
****[[Honduras]] signs an agreement with [[Pfizer]] and [[BioNTech]] to purchase additional 2.7 million doses of the [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] in order to ensure the country will have enough supply to vaccinate all people over the age of 12 this year. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/honduras-buy-27-million-more-pfizer-covid-19-vaccine-doses-2021-08-27/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Pacific Islands Forum]]
**[[Kiribati]] confirms its decision to withdraw along with four other countries, the [[Federated States of Micronesia]], the [[Marshall Islands]], [[Palau]] and [[Nauru]]. Despite efforts by multiple countries to have the countries remain in the forum, Kiribati says that there is "no value" in staying if the agreement is not honored in regards to disagreements over the designation of [[Henry Puna]] as Secretary-General of the forum. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/450088/kiribati-restates-decision-to-leave-pacific-forum (RNZ)]
*[[Foreign relations of Argentina]], [[Foreign relations of Iran]]
**[[Argentina]] condemns "energetically" the designation of [[Mohsen Rezai]] in a ministerial rank in the government of [[Ebrahim Raisi]] in [[Iran]]. Yesterday, Argentina had renewed its condemnation of the designation of [[Ahmad Vahidi]] as minister of the interior. Both men are wanted by Argentina and [[Interpol]] over alleged connections with the 1994 [[AMIA bombing]]. The Foreign Ministry condemns Iran for its "affront to Argentine justice". [https://www.notimerica.com/politica/noticia-argentina-iran-argentina-condena-designacion-dos-ministros-iran-reclamados-participacion-atentado-20210826123507.html (Notimérica)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Gretchen Whitmer kidnapping plot]]
**Ty Garbin is sentenced to six years in prison and fined [[United States dollar|$]]2,500 for his role in the [[kidnapping]] plot of [[Michigan]] Governor [[Gretchen Whitmer]] last year. He is the first person to be sentenced in the [[Conspiracy (criminal)|conspiracy]], which includes thirteen other accused plotters who are currently awaiting [[trial]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-58337712 (BBC News)]
*Aftermath of the [[Fall of Kabul (2021)|fall of Kabul]], [[2021 Taliban offensive]]
**The [[Taliban]] announce the re-imposition of the public ban on [[music]] in [[Afghanistan]]. [[Zabiullah Mujahid]], the official spokesperson for the Taliban, expressed the hope that the Emirate would be able to "persuade people not to do such things instead of pressuring them." [https://www.msn.com/en-gb/entertainment/music/taliban-to-forbid-music-in-public-again/ar-AANKVOp?ocid=uxbndlbing (''The Daily Telegraph'')]
*Former [[Prime Minister of Mali]] [[Soumeylou Boubèye Maïga]] is arrested accused of corruption for his involvement in the purchase of a presidential plane in 2014. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/malis-former-prime-minister-arrested-over-corruption-claims-2021-08-26/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Pope]] [[Pope Francis|Francis]] appoints Italian nun [[Alessandra Smerilli]] as Secretary of the [[Dicastery for Promoting Integral Human Development]], becoming the first woman to do so. [https://www.vaticannews.va/en/pope/news/2021-08/pope-francis-appointment-secretary-dicastery-human-development.html (Vatican News)]
